status: complete — pericopes for chapters 1-9 and 30-31, thematic clusters for 10-29
note: Covers the nine discourse chapters. Chapters 10-29 are collections of independent couplets and do not submit to a pericope schema at all; see structural_note. Chapters 30-31 (Agur, Lemuel, the acrostic) are discourse-shaped and can be indexed on this pattern, but are held until the couplet question is settled so the whole book is finished under one method rather than two.
structural_note: Proverbs 1-9 is continuous instruction — a father to a son, and Wisdom calling in the street — and indexes exactly like James or Jonah. Proverbs 10-29 is roughly 600 free-standing couplets in no narrative or argumentative order. Indexed at the density used for the first two books, that section alone would produce several hundred single-verse entries, most of them near-duplicates, and the index would become longer and less usable than the text it serves. That section needs a cluster entry — one entry gathering non-contiguous verses on a single theme — which the current schema cannot express, since it assumes one contiguous range per entry. That is a real decision about what the index is, not a formatting detail, and it is left open here deliberately.

entries.pericope: The purpose of the collection
entries.connection: The book states its own aim before saying anything else: not information but wise dealing, and prudence given to the simple. Wisdom is presented from the first line as a competence to be acquired, which is the premise C02 rests on.

entries.pericope: The fear of Yahweh is the beginning of knowledge
entries.connection: The entrance requirement, already load-bearing in C02. Knowledge has a doorway and the doorway is a posture, which is why the road cannot begin with technique.

entries.pericope: If sinners entice you; the ambush that catches its own
entries.connection: The Two Ways given as a recruitment scene — one purse, one company, one road. The trap closes on the people who set it, which is C01's claim that the Way of Death is self-executing rather than externally punished.

entries.pericope: Wisdom cries in the street, and is refused
entries.connection: Wisdom is not hidden. She shouts at the city gates and is ignored, and the consequence is eating the fruit of one's own way. The first anchor for C06: the eyes are not opened by information becoming available, because it already was.

entries.pericope: Seek her as silver, search as for hidden treasure
entries.connection: A conditional with the effort placed entirely on the near side — receive, store, turn the ear, call out, seek, search — and understanding on the far side. Wisdom is given by God and searched out by the man, and the passage refuses to resolve that tension.

entries.pericope: Discretion will watch over you
entries.connection: Wisdom entering the heart is described as posting a guard — discretion watching, understanding keeping. Watchfulness presented not as vigilance the person supplies but as what interior wisdom does once it is there.

entries.pericope: Don't let kindness and truth forsake you
entries.connection: The pairing this entire road is named for. Hesed and emet are bound together at the neck and written on the tablet of the heart — held as one thing, worn where they can be seen, and inscribed where they cannot. The instruction is not to practice mercy and truth alternately but to refuse to let either leave.

entries.pericope: Trust with all your heart; don't lean on your own understanding
entries.connection: Already load-bearing in C02. The Discipline of Unknowing in its plainest form: not that understanding is worthless, but that leaning on it is the error. Verse 7 names the failure exactly — being wise in one's own eyes.

entries.pericope: Honor Yahweh with your substance and firstfruits
entries.connection: Giving from the first of the increase rather than from what remains after. Habitual Almsgiving grounded in sequence rather than in amount, which is what makes it a habit and not a response to surplus.

entries.pericope: Whom Yahweh loves, he reproves
entries.connection: Correction reframed as evidence of relationship rather than of rejection. Necessary before the Moral Audit can be survivable — a man who reads reproof as condemnation will not look in the mirror twice.

entries.pericope: She is a tree of life; by wisdom Yahweh founded the earth
entries.connection: Wisdom valued above silver, then immediately identified as the instrument of creation itself. The same faculty that orders a life ordered the world, which is the continuity the Landscape of Wonder depends on.

entries.pericope: Then you shall walk securely; your sleep will be sweet
entries.connection: The reward of kept wisdom described as unafraid sleep and a foot that does not stumble. The first anchor for C10 — remaining is not strain but the ease that follows it.

entries.pericope: Don't say to your neighbor, come again tomorrow
entries.connection: Good withheld when it is already in the power of the hand to give. Delay named as its own offense, which is what separates Spontaneous Service from generosity in principle. The first anchor for C13.

entries.pericope: He gives grace to the humble
entries.connection: The verse James 4:6 and 1 Peter 5:5 both quote, in its original setting. Grace described as directed by posture, which is the whole architecture of the Hidden Life.
entries.review: PR13 retained after author review. The drafter argued these were a name-reading error and the reviewer marked all three sound; the author reversed the removal on reflection. The Hidden Life is read here as reaching the whole posture — the low place held without display, which is what grace is said to be given to — not only unsupervised work.

entries.pericope: Get wisdom, though it costs all your possessions
entries.connection: Instruction handed down a third generation — the father teaching what his own father taught him. Wisdom presented as inherited and as purchased, and the price named as everything.

entries.pericope: The path of the righteous is like the dawning light
entries.connection: Already load-bearing in C25. Growth described as increasing illumination rather than as arrival, and the contrast is not darkness that hurts but darkness that hides what one is stumbling over.

entries.pericope: Keep your heart with all diligence
entries.connection: The central text of C20 and the most cited verse of this book in the curriculum. The heart is guarded because it is the source, and what follows — the mouth, the eyes, the feet — is ordered outward from it in exactly that sequence.

entries.pericope: Her lips drip honey; the bitterness at the end
entries.connection: A trajectory traced from the sweetness at the start to the groaning at the latter end, with the regret given in the man's own voice. Interior Diagnosis run forward instead of backward: the beginning is judged by where it arrives.

entries.pericope: Drink water from your own cistern
entries.connection: Fidelity argued positively — satisfaction located in what one already has rather than restraint imposed on what one wants. The first anchor for C14, and the reason the household is treated there as a good rather than a limit.

entries.pericope: If you have become collateral for your neighbor
entries.connection: Urgent extrication from an obligation entered carelessly, with humbling oneself named as the means. Notable for treating a financial entanglement as a spiritual emergency, which is the stewardship logic the curriculum applies to money elsewhere.

entries.pericope: Go to the ant, you sluggard
entries.connection: The ant works without chief, overseer, or ruler, and poverty arrives by increments of a little slumber. Ordinary Faithfulness in its plainest form: work that no one is watching and no one will praise.
entries.review: PR20 removed at review. The reviewer was right and the error was the drafter's: PR20 is breaking a routine for a guest, not keeping one unsupervised. The tag was assigned from the practice's name without checking its definition.

entries.pericope: Seven things which are an abomination
entries.connection: A vice list running from haughty eyes to sowing discord among brothers, with the last given the emphatic position. The catalogue form C01 shares with the Didache's Way of Death, and the placement of discord last is not incidental.

entries.pericope: The commandment is a lamp; can a man scoop fire into his lap?
entries.connection: Teaching that walks with a man, watches while he sleeps, and speaks when he wakes — Watchfulness described as continuous rather than episodic. The fire and the coals then make the argument physical: some consequences are structural, not imposed.

entries.pericope: The young man void of understanding, watched from the window
entries.connection: The one extended narrative in this section, and the fall is located early — at the corner, in the twilight, before anyone speaks to him. The failure is a route taken, not a decision made, which is why C20 posts the watchman upstream of the moment of choice.

entries.pericope: Wisdom calls where the paths meet
entries.connection: Wisdom stationed at crossroads and city gates rather than in a sanctuary, claiming plainness as her own credential. Her words are said to be clear to whoever understands, which is the fruit test of C08 applied to speech before it is applied to teachers.

entries.pericope: I was the craftsman by his side, rejoicing before him
entries.connection: Wisdom present at the founding of the world and delighting in it daily. The strongest cosmological anchor in the Hebrew Scriptures for C24: the order a person is being formed into is the same order the world was made by.

entries.pericope: Watching daily at my gates
entries.connection: Blessing attached to daily waiting at the door rather than to a single act of finding. The Daily Anchors argued from the side of desire — the man is stationed there because he wants to be.

entries.pericope: Wisdom has built her house and set her table
entries.connection: Wisdom prepares a meal and sends her maidens to call in the simple by name. The invitation goes specifically to those who lack understanding, which sets the direction of the whole road: it is addressed to the unformed, not the qualified.

entries.pericope: Reprove a wise man and he will love you
entries.connection: Correction is triaged by the hearer rather than owed to everyone equally — reproving a mocker buys only insult. A restraint on rebuke that Covering Weakness needs, and one of the few places Scripture instructs a person to withhold a true word.
entries.review: PR17 removed on audit. PR17 is protecting someone from public embarrassment by absorbing the inconvenience oneself. This passage concerns triage of whom correction will profit, which is a different act. The tag was assigned from the practice's name — the fourth instance of that error, and the one that exposed three more.

entries.pericope: Folly calls from her seat, using the same words
entries.connection: Folly sits at her door and calls the simple in language identical to Wisdom's, changing nothing but what is on the table. The counterfeit is deliberate and near-perfect, which is why C07 treats cleansed sight as prior to good judgment rather than as a product of it.

entries.pericope: The tongue
entries.connection: The largest single theme in the collection. Speech is treated as an instrument with a physical effect — piercing or healing, kindling or starving a fire — and restraint is repeatedly named as the mark of understanding rather than of timidity. Both the guarding of C20 and the peacemaking of C15 draw on it.

entries.pericope: Generosity to the poor
entries.connection: Giving described as increase rather than depletion, and treatment of the poor read as treatment of their Maker. The lending-to-Yahweh image gives Habitual Almsgiving a warrant stronger than duty, and the shut ear that goes unanswered gives it a cost.

entries.ref: Proverbs · Pride and the low place
entries.pericope: Pride and the low place
entries.connection: Humility placed before honour as a matter of sequence, not reward — the low place comes first or the honour does not come. 25:6-7 gives the principle its scene: better to be told come up here than to be moved down in front of everyone.
entries.review: 25:6-7 added on synthesis review. The reviewer proposed it as the Old Testament source for PR25, and the verses plainly belong in this cluster — but PR25 was declined. PR25 is watching for the poor, the elderly and the stranger and giving up your own seat to them; 25:6-7 is prudent self-placement, which is the other half of the same scene and not the practice.

entries.pericope: Slow to anger
entries.connection: Ruling one's own spirit rated above taking a city, and overlooking an offense named as glory rather than as weakness. Absorbing the Blow argued from strength, and the broken-walled city gives the alternative its picture.

entries.pericope: Diligence and the sluggard
entries.connection: Steady unremarkable work set against the sluggard, who is portrayed as wise in his own eyes and hinged to his bed. The Hidden Life in its ordinary register — faithfulness no one supervises and no one applauds.
entries.review: PR20 removed. The same name-not-definition error corrected in Proverbs 6:6-11 had been repeated here; the cluster section was outside the reviewer's scope, so nothing external caught it. PR13 substituted, which the definition supports.

entries.pericope: Honest weights
entries.connection: The scale returned to four separate times, always as something God is directly concerned with. Commerce treated as a moral instrument rather than a neutral one, which is the ground the curriculum stands on when it addresses stewardship.

entries.pericope: Correction received
entries.connection: The capacity to hear reproof treated as the dividing line between the wise and the rest. Open rebuke rated above hidden love, and concealment of sin named as the thing that forecloses mercy — the Moral Audit's precondition and the Failure Recovery Protocol's door.

entries.pericope: The heart's own witness
entries.connection: The most sustained treatment of self-deception in Scripture: every way of a man is clean in his own eyes, and the way that seems right ends in death. The reason the Moral Audit cannot be conducted by consulting one's own impressions, and the reason C07 puts cleansed sight before judgment.

entries.pericope: Strife contained
entries.connection: Quarrel described hydraulically — a breach let loose, water that cannot be recalled — with the counsel always to stop it early. Covering an offense is named as seeking love, which is the plainest scriptural warrant for Covering Weakness.

entries.pericope: Plans and providence
entries.connection: A man plans his course and his steps are directed; many plans in the heart, and one counsel that stands. The Discipline of Unknowing applied to intention rather than to doctrine, and it does not forbid planning — only certainty about it.

entries.pericope: Mercy to the enemy
entries.connection: Repayment refused, gladness at an enemy's fall forbidden, and food and water commanded in their place. The Hebrew Scriptures anticipating the Sermon on the Mount by centuries, and the strongest anchor in this book for Non-Retaliation.

entries.pericope: Loyalty and the friend
entries.connection: Friendship defined by adversity rather than by affinity, and the wounds of a friend rated above an enemy's kisses. Unobligated Loyalty grounded here: the friend who sticks closer than a brother is bound by nothing but choice.

entries.pericope: Surely I am the most ignorant man
entries.connection: The oracle opens by disclaiming wisdom and knowledge, then asks four questions no one can answer — who gathered the wind, who bound the waters. The Discipline of Unknowing stated as a credential rather than a confession, and the warning against adding to God's words follows directly from it.

entries.pericope: Give me neither poverty nor riches
entries.connection: The only prayer in the book, and it asks for a bounded portion — enough food, no more — with the reason given for both directions: fullness produces denial, want produces theft. Holy Detachment argued as a request rather than a discipline, and it treats one's own likely failure as the thing to plan around.

entries.pericope: A generation pure in their own eyes, yet not washed
entries.connection: Four generations catalogued, and the second is self-acquittal — pure in their own eyes and not washed from their filthiness. The Moral Audit shown failing at the same point Proverbs 20:9 and 21:2 name, with the verdict reached before the looking.

entries.pericope: Three things never satisfied; four that don't say enough
entries.connection: The leech's two daughters cry give, give, and the list that follows is of appetites with no terminus. Holy Detachment argued from the structure of wanting rather than from the worth of what is wanted.

entries.pericope: She eats and wipes her mouth and says, I have done nothing wrong
entries.connection: Four wonders whose tracks cannot be traced, and then a fifth that is not wonderful at all: a wrong done and immediately erased in the doer's own account. The audit defeated not by concealment from others but by a clean conscience arrived at too quickly.

entries.pericope: Four things little on the earth, but exceedingly wise
entries.connection: Ants without strength, conies without power, locusts without a king, a lizard in a palace — each described by what it lacks and then by what it accomplishes anyway. The Hidden Life in its smallest register: work done without oversight, and wisdom located in the doing rather than in the capacity.
entries.review: PR20 assigned in drafting and removed by the drafter before publication. It is the third time this passage type has pulled PR20 in — after 6:6-11 and the 'Diligence and the sluggard' cluster, both corrected earlier in this same book — and it was made after the known-attractor note naming PR20 had already been written into the review brief. PR13 substituted: unsupervised faithfulness is what the four creatures actually show.

entries.pericope: Put your hand over your mouth
entries.connection: If you have exalted yourself or merely thought evil, stop the mouth. The final image is mechanical — churning produces butter, wringing produces blood, forcing wrath produces strife — so restraint is presented as the interruption of a process already running.

entries.pericope: Open your mouth for the mute
entries.connection: A king is told what to do with his voice: not to spend it on drink, and to spend it on those who have none. Speech treated as an office held on behalf of the desolate, and the instruction comes from his mother.

entries.pericope: She opens her arms to the poor; her works praise her in the gates
entries.connection: Twenty-two verses of ordinary labour — wool, flax, a field, a lamp burning late — with the reach to the poor set inside the household economy rather than beside it. The book ends not on a maxim but on a portrait, and what is praised is the fruit of her hands rather than her character described in the abstract.

schema_note: Two entry kinds. A pericope entry has a single contiguous 'ref'. A cluster entry has 'kind':'cluster' and a 'refs' array of non-contiguous verses gathered by theme, used for the aphorism collections where couplets on one subject are scattered across twenty chapters. A cluster claims thematic coverage, not verse coverage: verses not gathered into any cluster are not thereby judged to anchor nothing.

review_log.adjudication: Both flags accepted; both were the same error — PR20 assigned from the practice's name rather than its definition. The cluster instance had already been found and corrected independently while auditing, so the reviewer confirms it rather than discovering it. A proposed removal of PR13 from the grace-to-humility entries was raised by the drafter, rejected by the reviewer, and finally declined by the author; those tags stand.
Clean pass. PR21 proposed on 31:1-9 and declined. The drafter's own PR20 correction on 30:24-28 was independently confirmed.

method_rule: Practice tags are assigned from the definition in the Praxis Appendix, never from the practice's name. PR20 means breaking one's routine for a guest — the routine is what is given up — and read from the name alone it appears to mean the opposite.
